scope: Independent quality review of B41, B44, and B47. Source is ISO 32000-2:2020 + EC3 held in this worktree. Test histories are records only; no tests were run for this review.

features.source_locator: EC3 primary physical p.599 / printed p.584. The paragraph requires current-UTC revocation checking on every timestamp-unit path certificate; known keyCompromise, cACompromise, or missing reason makes token time unusable. No relevant EC3 annotation appears on physical p.599.
features.implementation: viewer-core/src/notes.rs::signature_timestamps_instant promotes every Time::Established { at, .. } to the best-signature time. pdf-signature::timestamp::signature_timestamp_established retains the timestamp path's revocation result in Time::Established but the consumer ignores it.
features.test_quality: notes/timestamp_revocation_spec_audit.rs calls the actual private time-selection consumer. It uses real CAdES CMS with a signature timestamp attribute; asserts the token imprint covers the actual SignerInfo.signature; checks a Good CRL positive control, a root-signed current CRL listing the TSA for KeyCompromise, and a tampered-CRL Unknown control before the failing selector expectation. The README records independent OpenSSL verification of CMS, RFC 3161 token, TSA/document chains and CRLs. Fixed genTime/verification instants are 2026-11-16 16:12:23Z and 17:12:23Z, with both certs valid through 2036 and CRL windows covering both times.
features.verdict: RETAIN WITH SCOPE QUALIFICATION. The tested selector uses a genTime despite a known keyCompromise at the required current-time TSA check, contrary to the explicit §12.8.3.4.8 rule. This is a direct consumer-level selection witness, not a full public Report or final signer verdict test. The helper test independently validates the token/TSA material and its imprint but does not assert outer CMS authenticity within Rust; the committed fixture README records successful independent OpenSSL verification of the outer CMS as well. Do not claim all revoked/unknown TSA statuses invalidate a timestamp.
features.adr_relevance: ADR 1071's document-timestamp chain rules do not resolve the signature-attribute-specific reason gate. ADR 1067 correctly preserves a known Revoked result; that result must remain available to this time-selection decision. ADR 1112 establishes BestSignatureTime but does not override the explicit reason-specific .4.8 rule.
features.limits: No complete Command::Report/fallback assertion, no UI language claim, and no claim about document-timestamp-chain reason handling.

features.source_locator: EC3 primary physical p.598 / printed p.583. For a current-time check, a CRL is appropriate only when current UTC is within the thisUpdate-to-nextUpdate period. No relevant EC3 annotation appears on physical p.598.
features.implementation: The public Report route has no trusted timestamp in these PDFs and supplies host current time 1794848986 (2026-11-16 17:09:46Z). revocation::from_list checks signature/issuer and nextUpdate but not at >= thisUpdate; notes::signatures passes host time into Signature::trust.
features.test_quality: current_crl_report_spec_audit.rs exercises Open, Trust, and public Command::Report. It guards exact-xref/no-recovery parsing and requires ByteRange digest, RSA verification and SigningCertificateV2 signer binding in both branches. Host time, root/leaf, PDF structure and nextUpdate are shared. The signed CRL control has thisUpdate 17:08:46Z; the test target's has thisUpdate 17:10:46Z, both with nextUpdate 2027-01-15 17:09:46Z. Leaf validity spans the host instant. The in-window Report is locally valid; the historical run record says the future-thisUpdate Report is also called locally valid. Parent independently checked both ByteRanges, CMS, chain at host time, CRLs and qpdf syntax.
features.verdict: RETAIN. This is a strong public PAdES current-time witness to the explicit .4.7 condition. Qualify it as a context-specific PAdES/current-time gap, not a global rule for generic status() calls. The historical .4.8 clause expressly uses a different CRL condition; do not break later-issued evidence for historical validation.
features.adr_relevance: ADR 1112 deliberately adopted EN 319 102-1's one-ended freshness semantics in shared generic CRL code, with the rationale that later-issued material can answer a proven historical time. The new current-time public test shows the rationale cannot be extended to .4.7's explicit interval. Keep the historical rule, but distinguish current PAdES checks. ADRs 1067 and 2775 retain their separate evidence and policy roles; neither supplies a reason to erase .4.7's current interval.
features.limits: No claim that all certificate status APIs should reject future thisUpdate; no network retrieval or external trust-store claim. The held ISO text establishes the finding; external EN 319 102-1 was not independently re-audited from a local copy.

features.source_locator: EC3 primary physical p.599 / printed p.584. Historical OCSP is appropriate only if captured before signer-certificate expiry and its signed producedAt is after the trusted past UTC time. No relevant EC3 annotation appears on physical p.599.
features.implementation: revocation::from_response retains BasicResponse.produced_at but its Good branch tests responder authorization, SingleResponse thisUpdate/nextUpdate and status without comparing producedAt with the validation instant. The public notes/report path supplies the established CAdES timestamp time as historical validation time.
features.test_quality: historical_ocsp_report_spec_audit.rs exercises public Command::Report with the same signed PDF revision, CAdES signature, RFC 3161 token, anchors, host time and TSA Good CRL in both branches. Both issuer-signed OCSP responses say Good and have thisUpdate < T < nextUpdate. At trusted T=2026-11-16 17:09:09Z, early producedAt is 17:09:06Z and late is 17:09:11Z; their windows are 16:59:06–18:09:06Z and 16:59:11–18:09:11Z respectively, so both satisfy the window predicate and are not asserted identical. Shared helper assertions require ByteRange digest, CMS RSA signature, signer binding, timestamp imprint and the report's historical time before checking local validity. The recorded run says late control passes and early response still yields local validity. Parent independently verified the actual ByteRanges, CMS/token/imprint, OCSP signatures/CertID/status, paths and CRL; qpdf checked syntax.
features.capture_before_expiry_qualification: The paired response/PDF fixtures were generated in 2026 while the signer certificate is valid through 2036. That makes the fixed fixture's construction occur before expiry, but the appended DSS revision itself has no trusted timestamp proving capture time to a reader. producedAt is not the capture-time proof; this finding isolates the separate explicit producedAt predicate and does not claim capture-before-expiry is enforced for arbitrary inputs.
features.verdict: RETAIN WITH CAPTURE-TIME LIMIT. The early/late public pair is a meaningful controlled witness for the explicit producedAt > historical-time condition; both status windows bracket T and controls require the actual trusted token time. The test does not establish the separate capture-before-expiry provenance condition for arbitrary documents, and must not equate producedAt with capture.
features.adr_relevance: ADR 1112's one-ended freshness rule governs issuance freshness; it does not establish the distinct BasicOCSPResponse producedAt predicate. ADR 1071's timestamp-chain establishment and ADR 1067's revocation material handling do not remove this .4.8 condition. ADR 2775 distinguishes OCSP SingleResponse thisUpdate from response-level producedAt, supporting the feature distinction without proving capture time.
features.limits: No full-clause .4.8 certification; no general assertion that response producedAt authenticates when its DSS bytes were captured.

local_external_sources: The licensed EC3 primary PDF and markdown are present and were inspected. No local RFC 6960, ETSI EN 319 102-1, or other external standards copy was found in this worktree; the review does not independently assess those external texts or let them override an explicit ISO condition.
